title: camelCase and snake_case conversion with acronyms
description: Implement camel_to_snake(name) and snake_to_camel(name, upper_first=False); both require a str (TypeError). camel_to_snake lowercases the name and inserts '_' at word boundaries: between a lowercase letter or digit and a following uppercase letter ('fooBar' gives 'foo_bar', 'v2Beta' gives 'v2_beta', 'base64Encode' gives 'base64_encode'), and between an acronym and the capitalised word that follows it ('HTTPServer' gives 'http_server', 'parseXMLFile' gives 'parse_xml_file'). Digits stay attached to the letters before them ('ipV4' gives 'ip_v4'). Underscores already in the input are kept and an '_' is never inserted next to an existing '_' ('foo_Bar' gives 'foo_bar'). snake_to_camel splits on '_' and ignores empty parts (so leading, trailing and doubled underscores vanish); every part is lowercased first; the first part stays lowercase (or is capitalised when upper_first is true) and each later part gets an uppercase first letter ('http_server' gives 'httpServer', 'HTTP_SERVER' gives 'httpServer', 'a_1_b' gives 'a1B'). Empty string returns ''.
invariants: No doubled underscores: 'foo_Bar' -> 'foo_bar'; existing underscores are kept ('already_snake' unchanged).
snake_to_camel lowercases every part before capitalising, drops empty parts, and honours upper_first.
